mainTopic: The bakers' exemptions from tithing דמאי, the short terms of the מקדש שני's כהנים גדולים, and why שילה was destroyed
overview: This amud finishes the גמרא's discussion of bakers (נחתומים) who bought דמאי grain from an עם הארץ. They need not separate תרומה גדולה, because יוחנן כהן גדול found that everyone already separated it. They need not give מעשר ראשון or מעשר עני, because a לוי or poor person must prove the grain was untithed (המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה). The גמרא then challenges: why not require מעשר שני, which goes to no one else? עולא answers that government officials (פרהדרין, explained as פורסי) pressured the bakers all year to sell cheaply, so the רבנן did not burden them further. Next, רבי יוחנן reads a פסוק in משלי as a contrast. The מקדש ראשון stood 410 years with only 18 כהנים גדולים, while the מקדש שני stood 420 years with over 300, so apart from a few צדיקים, none of them finished a year. Finally, רבי יוחנן בן תורתא teaches that שילה was destroyed for גילוי עריות and בזיון קדשים, and the גמרא brings a פסוק about בני עלי. It then notes רבי יוחנן's view that בני עלי did not literally sin, and begins an explanation that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why bakers need not separate תרומה גדולה
steps.stepSummary: The bakers are exempt from תרומה גדולה because יוחנן כהן גדול found that all of Israel already separated it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he (יוחנן כהן גדול) sent messengers throughout all the borders of Israel, and he saw that people were separating only תרומה גדולה and nothing else.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the middle of an answer. The גמרא is explaining why bakers who buy דמאי grain do not have to separate תרומה גדולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוחנן כהן גדול checked the whole land and found that even an עם הארץ always separated תרומה גדולה, though not the tithes. That is why he decreed that buyers must tithe דמאי produce. However, תרומה גדולה was never in doubt, so the bakers never have to separate it.

keyTerms.meaning: The borders or regions of ארץ ישראל
They separate (set aside the required portions)
The 'great' תרומה: the first gift from the crop, given to a כהן
Produce bought from an עם הארץ that may not have been tithed

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'he' here refers to יוחנן כהן גדול, who is named in the earlier part of the sugya. He is not the אמורא רבי יוחנן who appears later here.

phrases.english: Because he sent messengers throughout all the borders of Israel,
phrases.notes: The subject is יוחנן כהן גדול.

phrases.english: and he saw that they do not separate
anything except the great terumah alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an explanation that began on the previous amud, about the baker's limited obligation with דמאי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Everyone already separates תרומה גדולה, so there is no doubt about it with דמאי grain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bakers are exempt from separating תרומה גדולה from דמאי.

steps.title: Why bakers need not give מעשר ראשון or מעשר עני
steps.stepSummary: The bakers are exempt from מעשר ראשון and מעשר עני because a Levite or poor person must prove the grain was untithed before he can take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And מעשר ראשון and מעשר עני are also not required, because whoever wants to take something from his friend must bring the proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues down the list of gifts. It explains why the bakers also do not need to give מעשר ראשון or מעשר עני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two tithes are not holy food. They are simply money owed to a לוי or a poor person. Since the grain is only doubtfully untithed, the לוי or poor person would have to prove it was really untithed, under the rule המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה. This step sets up the contrast that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: First tithe, given to a לוי
Poor man's tithe, given to the poor in certain years
One who wants to take from his fellow must bring proof

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה is a basic principle of monetary law across all of ש״ס. Here it is applied to tithes, which are owed like money.

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן וּמַעְשַׂר עָנִי נָמֵי לָא,
phrases.english: First tithe and poor man's tithe are also not required,
because one who takes from his fellow bears the burden of proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן וּמַעְשַׂר עָנִי נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the granted premise from תרומה גדולה to the non-holy tithes. This completes the setup that the גמרא then challenges in step 3 regarding מעשר שני.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bakers are exempt from מעשר ראשון and מעשר עני on דמאי, because the לוי or poor person would have to prove the grain was untithed (המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה).

steps.title: Why not require מעשר שני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling: מעשר שני belongs to the owner and has no claimant, so why aren't the bakers required to separate it and eat it in ירושלים?
steps.simpleTranslation: But מעשר שני? Let them separate it, bring it up, and eat it in ירושלים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty. The burden-of-proof answer does not work for מעשר שני, so why are the bakers exempt from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני is not given to anyone else. The owner eats it himself in ירושלים, so there is no other person who needs to bring proof. Anyone else who buys דמאי must separate מעשר שני, so the bakers' exemption seems unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, eaten by the owner in ירושלים
And let them bring it up (to ירושלים)

phrases.english: But second tithe?
Let them separate it and bring it up
and eat it in Jerusalem!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the reason given in step 2 does not cover מעשר שני.
steps.kashyaTarget: The bakers' exemption from מעשר שני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The burden-of-proof reason only works for gifts that go to another person. מעשר שני stays with the owner, so it should still be required, as it is for every other buyer of דמאי.

steps.title: עולא: the bakers were already pressured by officials
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that government officials pressured the bakers all year to sell cheaply, so the רבנן did not add the burden of מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Because these פרהדרין (officials) beat the bakers all twelve months and tell them, 'Sell cheap! Sell cheap!', the רבנן did not burden them further.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the challenge. He explains that the exemption is a special leniency for the bakers' hard situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tithing דמאי is only a חומרא (stringency), since most people do tithe. The bakers could not raise their prices to make up for lost grain and trips to ירושלים. So the רבנן chose not to impose this rabbinic burden on them. This is an exception for bakers; it does not cancel the general law of דמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages did not burden them

steps.whatToRemember: Bakers buying דמאי are exempt from תרומה גדולה (everyone already gives it), from מעשר ראשון and מעשר עני (the claimant must bring proof), and from מעשר שני (the רבנן did not burden the pressured bakers).
steps.whyThisMatters: The 'twelve months' term of the פרהדרין connects back to the larger סוגיא. There, the כהנים גדולים of the מקדש שני are compared to these officials, who were replaced every year.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Because these government officials

phrases.aramaic: חוֹבְטִין אוֹתָן כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: beat them (the bakers) all twelve months,
and say to them:
Sell cheaply! Sell cheaply!
the Sages did not burden them further.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about מעשר שני.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bakers should be required to separate מעשר שני like any buyer of דמאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the bakers were financially pressured and tithing דמאי is only a stringency, the רבנן exempted them.

steps.title: Defining the word פרהדרין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what פרהדרין means and answers: פורסי, royal appointees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain an unusual word that עולא used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פרהדרין is a foreign word. The גמרא translates it as פורסי, officials appointed by the government for set terms. This is only a definition; it does not change the law.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean?

phrases.english: What are parhedrin?
Royal appointees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines a term used in עולא's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word פרהדרין

steps.title: The מקדש ראשון had few, long-serving כהנים גדולים
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק 'יראת ה׳ תוסיף ימים' as describing the מקדש ראשון: it stood 410 years with only 18 כהנים גדולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is the meaning of the פסוק, 'The fear of ה׳ adds days, but the years of the wicked will be shortened'? 'The fear of ה׳ adds days' refers to the מקדש ראשון. It stood for 410 years, and only 18 כהנים גדולים served in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new teaching that interprets a פסוק from משלי. This step explains the first half of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eighteen כהנים גדולים over 410 years means each one served a long time. That shows the righteousness of that era: 'fear of ה׳ adds days.' Step 7 applies the second half of the פסוק, about the wicked, to the מקדש שני.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties into the סוגיא's theme. In the מקדש שני, כהנים גדולים were replaced constantly, like the yearly פרהדרין. Steps 7 and 8 draw the contrast with the מקדש ראשון.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"The fear of the Lord prolongs days,
but the years of the wicked will be shortened"?

phrases.aramaic: ״יִרְאַת ה׳ תּוֹסִיף יָמִים״ זֶה מִקְדָּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן
phrases.english: "The fear of the Lord prolongs days": this is the First Temple,
which stood four hundred and ten years,
and there served in it
only eighteen High Priests,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new אגדה teaching related to the מקדש שני theme of short-serving כהנים גדולים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first half of the פסוק describes the מקדש ראשון, whose 18 כהנים גדולים served long terms across 410 years.

steps.title: The second half of the פסוק describes the מקדש שני
steps.stepSummary: ״וּשְׁנוֹת רְשָׁעִים תִּקְצֹרְנָה״ refers to the מקדש שני. It stood 420 years and had more than 300 כהנים גדולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'But the years of the wicked will be shortened': this is the מקדש שני. It stood for four hundred and twenty years, and more than three hundred כהנים גדולים served in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the same teaching from step 6 and explains the second half of the פסוק. The first half was about the מקדש ראשון; this half is about the מקדש שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two halves of the פסוק make a contrast. The מקדש ראשון had 410 years and only 18 כהנים גדולים, so each served a long time. The מקדש שני had 420 years but over 300 כהנים גדולים, so most of them served a very short time. Their 'shortened years' show they were not righteous.

phrases.english: 'But the years of the wicked will be shortened'
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the פסוק in משלי י:כז.

phrases.english: this is the Second Temple,
which stood for four hundred and twenty years

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁמְּשׁוּ בּוֹ יוֹתֵר מִשְּׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת כֹּהֲנִים.
phrases.english: and more than three hundred (High) Priests served in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁנוֹת רְשָׁעִים תִּקְצֹרְנָה זֶה מִקְדָּשׁ שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading of the פסוק begun in step 6 by explaining its second half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second half of the פסוק describes the מקדש שני, where over 300 כהנים גדולים served in 420 years.

steps.title: Doing the math: most כהנים גדולים didn't last a year
steps.stepSummary: Take away the long terms of a few righteous כהנים גדולים. That leaves too few years for the many remaining כהנים גדולים, so none of them completed even one year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Subtract from the total: forty years that שמעון הצדיק served, eighty years that יוחנן כהן גדול served, and ten years that ישמעאל בן פיאבי served. Some say also eleven years that רבי אלעזר בן חרסום served. From here on, go and calculate: not one of the rest finished his year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the arithmetic to prove that the כהנים גדולים of the מקדש שני had 'shortened years.' It removes the long terms of a few great כהנים and shows that the rest each served less than a year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forty, plus eighty, plus ten (plus eleven, by the other opinion) comes to 130 or 141 years. That leaves about 290 or 279 years. Those years had to be shared by close to 300 remaining כהנים גדולים, so on average each served less than a year. This proves the פסוק: the wicked ones were cut short.

keyTerms.meaning: A famous early כהן גדול of the מקדש שני
The כהן גדול who served 80 years

steps.whatToRemember: מקדש ראשון: 410 years, 18 כהנים גדולים, so long terms for righteous people. מקדש שני: 420 years, 300+ כהנים גדולים, so short terms. Apart from a few צדיקים, each one did not last a year.

phrases.english: Subtract from them forty years
that Shimon HaTzaddik served,
and eighty that Yochanan the High Priest served,
ten that Yishmael ben Pavi served,
and some say eleven
that Rabbi Elazar ben Charsum served,
from here onward, go out and calculate:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד לֹא הוֹצִיא שְׁנָתוֹ.
phrases.english: each and every one did not complete his year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 7's claim with a calculation.
steps.raayaObject: That the כהנים גדולים of the מקדש שני had 'shortened years.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: An arithmetic count: subtract the long terms of the righteous כהנים from 420 years and divide the rest among 300+ כהנים.

steps.title: Why שילה was destroyed: two sins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן תורתא teaches that the משכן in שילה was destroyed because of two sins: גילוי עריות and בזיון קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן תורתא said: Why was שילה destroyed? Because two things were there: forbidden relations and disrespect for holy offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new related teaching. Having discussed sinful כהנים, it now explains why the earlier holy place, the משכן in שילה, was destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן תורתא asks a question and answers it himself; it is all one statement. He names two specific sins as the cause. Step 10 brings the source for the first sin, גילוי עריות. The source for בזיון קדשים comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who taught about the reasons for the destructions
The place where the משכן stood before the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Torta said:
Why was Shiloh destroyed?
Because there were two things in it:
forbidden relations, and degradation of consecrated offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן תּוֹרְתָּא מִפְּנֵי מָה חָרְבָה שִׁילֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching connected by theme (sinful כהנים) to the discussion of the מקדש שני.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שילה was destroyed because of גילוי עריות and בזיון קדשים.

steps.title: פסוק proving גילוי עריות at שילה
steps.stepSummary: The proof for גילוי עריות is the פסוק that says the sons of עלי 'lay with the women' who gathered at the entrance of the אהל מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Forbidden relations, as it is written: 'Now עלי was very old, and he heard all that his sons were doing to all of Israel, and that they lay with the women who gathered at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from שמואל א to prove the first sin, גילוי עריות. The plain words of the פסוק describe בני עלי lying with women at the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the source for the first of the two sins named in step 9. Read simply, the פסוק says the sons of עלי committed forbidden relations right at the entrance of the holy place.

phrases.english: Forbidden relations, as it is written:
'Now Eli was very old

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁמַע אֵת כׇּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשׂוּן בָּנָיו לְכׇל יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: and he heard all that his sons were doing to all of Israel
and how they lay with the women
who gathered at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.'
phrases.notes: This comes from the פסוק in שמואל א ב:כב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the first sin named in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That there was גילוי עריות at שילה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א ב:כב, ״וְאֵת אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁכְּבוּן אֶת הַנָּשִׁים״.

steps.title: Acknowledging the view that בני עלי did not sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes a problem: רבי יוחנן said that anyone who says בני עלי sinned is simply mistaken. It begins explaining how the proof still works, starting with the word 'מתוך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'Anyone who says the sons of עלי sinned is simply mistaken,' [still,] because of...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible objection to the proof it just brought. It does not stop to argue; it immediately starts an explanation that continues on the next amud. This line is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בני עלי did not literally sin, how can the פסוק prove גילוי עריות at שילה? The word 'מתוך' ('because of') begins the answer. Even on רבי יוחנן's view, something they did was serious enough that the פסוק treats it as גילוי עריות.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often quotes רבי יוחנן

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is contradicting itself or dropping its proof. It admits that רבי יוחנן holds בני עלי did not literally sin. It is about to explain that the פסוק still counts their conduct as גילוי עריות. The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
phrases.english: And even though Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who says the sons of Eli sinned
is nothing other than mistaken,
[still,] because of
phrases.notes: Sentence continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible objection to the proof in step 10 and begins to answer it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of the פסוק in step 10 as proof of גילוי עריות at שילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן says בני עלי did not literally sin, so the פסוק seems unable to prove that גילוי עריות happened.
